name: Destructive button
purpose: Make destructive actions clearly distinguishable and readable without relying on colour alone, and without washed-out translucent red.
whenToUse: The confirm button of a destructive confirm dialog (Delete project).
A dedicated danger zone action in settings (Delete account) that opens a confirmation.
A menu item that removes or deletes something (text colour plus icon, last in the menu).
A low-risk, undoable removal where a quiet neutral destructive style is enough (Remove from list).
whenNotToUse: Ordinary, reversible actions such as Archive, Clear filters or Close. Use a neutral button.
As the main action of a view. The primary action is emerald; a destructive action is never primary.
Placed directly beside the primary button with the same emphasis. Pair a destructive button with a neutral Cancel instead.
More than one solid destructive button in the same view.
A pale red text on a translucent dark-red background (P19). That treatment is washed out and fails contrast.
An icon only red button with no label or accessible name.
anatomy: Container: solid --danger-solid fill, --r radius, --control-h height (40px for large).
Label: an explicit verb and object (Delete project), --danger-ink on the fill.
Optional leading icon (trash, 16px) before the label.
Loading: a spinner replaces the icon, the label becomes a progressive verb (Deleting), width stays stable.

variants.description: --danger-solid fill, white text, optional trash icon. Hover steps to --danger-solid-hover.
Neutral --s3 surface with --danger text and icon. No tinted fill.
variants.useWhen: Low-risk deletes, toolbars, the trigger that opens a confirm dialog.

variants.description: Menu item with --danger text and icon, last, after a separator.
variants.useWhen: Delete inside a context menu or overflow menu.

variants.description: Plain secondary button with a clear verb.
variants.useWhen: The action is reversible or has an Undo.

behavior: One solid destructive button per view. If two seem necessary, the second is neutral.
Never adjacent to the primary action in the same emphasis; pair it with Cancel.
Disabled: opacity 0.45, no pointer; do not remove the button, explain why nearby when it is not obvious.
Loading: aria-busy="true", spinner replaces the icon, repeat clicks are ignored until done.
High-impact destructive actions are confirmed in a dialog (see preset.confirm-dialog), with initial focus on Cancel.
In menus, danger items keep the shared menu hover fill; they never get a red background.
accessibility: Measured: white (--danger-ink) on --danger-solid is about 5.1:1 (hover state --danger-solid-hover is about 4.3:1, slightly under 4.5). --danger text on --s3 is about 4.75:1 but on --s4 only about 4.0:1, so the neutral and menu variants always pair the colour with a verb and an icon and should not be used for small text.
The action is named by a verb, not by colour; an icon supports the verb.
Use a real button element. When busy, set aria-busy and keep the label so the name does not change abruptly.
Disabled uses the disabled attribute (or aria-disabled when it must stay focusable).
Focus ring is the shared 1.5px neutral ring, not red.
